title: SC warns of ‘constitutional tort’ over protest-related hardship to traders, workers
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Friday warned that it could invoke its constitutional tort jurisdiction to award compensation if protests in Delhi disproportionately affect traders and daily-wage earners, expressing concern over the hardship faced by small businesses during the festive season.

Adding to this, A view CP Market during the in a Tiranga March on Friday. (RAJ K RAJ /HT PHOTO) A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi made the observations while hearing a plea raising concerns over the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) call for a gathering at Central Park in Connaught Place on Friday evening. The court hoped that “better sense will prevail” and that the competing interests of protesters, traders and authorities would be balanced.

Meanwhile, “If there is loss of business, if it is unlawful to your clients, we will exercise our powers under constitutional tort jurisdiction. Let’s cross that bridge when it comes,” justice Bagchi told advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai, who mentioned the petition on behalf of a traders’ association.

Notably, The observations came a day after the Delhi High Court recorded an assurance from Delhi Police that it would take “all possible measures under the law” to regulate the proposed gathering and address concerns over disruption to business and movement around Connaught Place.

As per the latest buzz, Dehadrai told the Supreme Court that the protest could cause substantial losses to traders, particularly during the festive season, when businesses depend on higher sales for a significant share of their annual earnings. He claimed that disruption around Connaught Place was causing losses of more than ₹ 250 crore rupees a day.

In further updates, Initially indicating that the matter would not be taken up immediately, CJI Kant shared, “This is also related to protest. It can wait till October 26.” Justice Bagchi pointed out that the Delhi High Court had heard a similar petition on Thursday.

On top of that, When counsel insisted that the Supreme Court plea raised distinct concerns, the judge shared the competing claims of protesters, traders and law enforcement agencies had to be considered together. “Someone wants to protest, someone wants to sell moongfali (peanuts), someone wants to maintain law and order. All are there before us. We can hear it after a week,” he shared.

The CJI expressed concern over the economic vulnerability of small traders and their families during the festive period. “We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers, they earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship, difficulty and crises entire families face,” he shared.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

title: Subhash Ghai says actors of this generation prioritise money over art, recalls how actors took 40% fees in his films
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Subhash Ghai has directed some of the most successful films in the 1980s and 90s, including Khalnayak, Hero, Pardes and Taal. The filmmaker has now reacted to how actors today prioritise money over their craft. In an interview with Screen, the filmmaker spoke about the change that has taken place in the industry.

Adding to this, Filmmaker Subhash Ghai spoke about the changing business of cinema. (PTI Photo) (PTI11_26_2024_000410B) (PTI) What Subhash Ghai shared The director shared, “Commerce has taken over. Today, the children want to earn more money, and it’s less about the art. During our time, the actors wanted to be artistes, and thought money will eventually come. Nobody would wait for the money. They would sign a movie based on the director, the story and the character. Most of the stars in my movies have taken only 40 per cent of the price because they were interested in the character and the story.”

Meanwhile, He added, "Today, if you ask any star to take only 40 per cent fees, four of their managers will intervene, and 3 PRs will come in together to endorse the star as a star. Today, there are various other means of earning for actors rather than just movies. But again, they are seasonal; the craze dies down after 3-4 years. Then they are out of the picture, and somebody else walks in.”

Notably, On Koffee with Karan Season 9, even Salman Khan brought out this issue in the movie industry. title: Press Council of India issues guidelines for journalists covering protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Press Council of India (PCI), a statutory and quasi-judicial body meant to preserve press freedom, has issued guidelines for journalists covering protests, emphasising professional conduct, crowd safety, ethical reporting and coordination with newsrooms and law enforcement agencies.

Adding to this, Many protesters have been dragged, manhandled and detained. (AP Photo) The guidelines were rolled out on Thursday to “facilitate orderly and effective media coverage of protests” while ensuring the safety of journalists and responsible reporting. They call on journalists to carry valid identity cards issued by their media organisations or applicable Press Information Bureau (PIB)/Directorate of Information and Publicity (DIP) accreditation. They ask journalists to keep their press identification clearly visible while reporting.

Meanwhile, The guidelines were issued against the backdrop of tens of thousands of people taking to the streets seeking chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s removal and the scrapping of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll. The authorities ordered Metro closures, Internet shutdowns, imposed prohibitory orders and deployed 40,000 security personnel to turn Delhi into a virtual fortress.
Notably, Many protesters were dragged, manhandled and detained. On Sunday, at least 12 journalists covering the second day of protests were detained.

As per the latest buzz, The PCI, which has jurisdiction only over print media under the Press Council Act of 1978, has advised journalists to secure their identity cards and lanyards carefully to prevent entanglement during crowd movement or confrontations. It emphasised professional neutrality and asked journalists not to participate in demonstrations, take sides, provoke confrontations or interfere with protesters, counterprotesters or police.

In further updates, The PCI advised media personnel to remain respectful, follow police orders and comply with lawful instructions issued for immediate safety, while calmly asserting their press status when necessary.

On top of that, The PCI asked journalists to maintain a reasonable distance from confrontations, particularly when tensions escalate, or police action is anticipated. It shared they should avoid attaching cameras or recording equipment to police barricades, vehicles, or other equipment in ways that could obstruct movement or cause damage.
The guidelines recommend careful movement through crowds and continuous assessment of potential dangers. They stressed the importance of situational awareness and escape planning.

title: Delhi Police ask Dipke to call off Connaught Place demonstration, say area is not a protest site
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police has prohibited CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke from holding any form of demonstration, procession or rally in the vicinity of Connaught Place, citing the need to protect public safety, traffic movement and the rights of citizens and traders.

Adding to this, A Delhi Police official with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, ahead of the party's 'Lehra Do Tiranga' rally. In a notice served to Dipke on Friday, Delhi Police told CJP founder that “Connaught Place is not a notified protest site and that demonstrations may be held at designated venues, subject to the necessary permission being sought and granted.” It further shared that such an “unlawful assembly” posed a serious risk to public order and infringed on the rights of other citizens.

Meanwhile, A prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is currently in force in the area and any violation could invite action under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and other applicable laws, police told Dipke.
Notably, “Not only has no permission been sought, but any unauthorised public gathering could critically imperil the factors mentioned by the Hon’ble Apex Court,” the notice shared.

As per the latest buzz, Delhi Police shared the event could disrupt traffic and affect businesses, including showrooms, restaurants, hotels, banks, offices and street vendors. Police, in the notice, also warned of possible congestion or a stampede near Rajiv Chowk Metro station, which caters to an average of two lakh commuters daily.

In further updates, “It (CP) houses a dense concentration of showrooms, restaurants, hotels, banks, offices and street vendors, so any disruption, particularly during evening and weekend hours, as well as the peak festival season, directly affects the livelihood of traders and their employees. Over 15 lakh traders and their employees depend on its peaceful and orderly functioning for the exercise of their fundamental right,” the notice read.

On top of that, Delhi Police shared several arterial roads pass through CP, and their obstruction could paralyse traffic across central Delhi. It also cited, in the notice, the area's proximity to Parliament, the Central Secretariat and diplomatic precincts, raising concerns about public order and security.
Police further shared narrow service lanes and older buildings could impede the movement of fire tenders and ambulances, potentially compromising emergency response services.

title: Ranbir Kapoor leases his luxury apartment in Pune’s Trump Towers for a monthly rent starting at ₹4.63 lakh
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Adding to this, Pune real estate market: Ranbir Kapoor has leased out his 6,094 sq ft luxury apartment at Trump Towers in Pune for a starting monthly rent of ₹4.6 lakh. (AFP) The leave and licence agreement for the apartment in Pune’s Kalyani Nagar, Yerwada area was registered on October 6, 2026, and the apartment was leased for three years, from September 20, 2026 to September 19, 2029, the documents show.

Meanwhile, According to the documents, the apartment has an approximate area of 6,094 sq ft and includes three covered car parking spaces. As per the latest buzz, Ranbir Kapoor could not be reached for comment.

In further updates, The Trump Organisation tied up with Pune's Panchshil Realty to construct Trump Towers in Pune’s Kalyani Nagar area a decade ago. The development in Pune consists of two 23-story towers, each with 46 single-floor apartments. The 46 apartments are ready to move in and spread across 3.69 lakh sq ft. The project comprises 5.5 BHK apartments.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay-led TVK has joined the Opposition’s protest in Chennai against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan shared on Friday.

Adding to this, The TVK joined the INDIA bloc’s protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) leader Thol. Thirumavalavan shared. (@ncbn X) Speaking about TVK’s participation in the protest on October 15, Thirumavalavan shared the party had of late joined the INDIA bloc ’s Tamil Nadu unit and was expected to participate in similar protests at the national level in the future.

Meanwhile, “TVK has already joined the INDIA bloc. They are against the Election Commission and the Union government. They attended the INDIA bloc protest yesterday. Of late, they have joined the Tamil Nadu unit; later on, they will participate in the protest at the national level,” he told ANI.

Notably, The protest was organised against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, an exercise to review and update voter lists. Opposition parties have raised concerns that the process could lead to the deletion of eligible voters’ names and demanded safeguards to protect voting rights.

As per the latest buzz, The demonstration also included a demand for the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar , with opposition parties questioning the Election Commission’s handling of electoral matters.

In further updates, TVK’s participation in the protest follows a series of political engagements with opposition parties in Tamil Nadu. title: Nitanshi Goel joins Korean skincare brand Mamonde as its first India brand ambassador
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nitanshi captured the country’s attention with her breakout performance in Laapataa Ladies, winning hearts with her charm and natural screen presence. Now, she is stepping into the world of Korean beauty with Mamonde, a brand that pairs skincare science with the power of flowers. With young Indian consumers increasingly looking to K-beauty for innovative formulations and effective skincare, the partnership brings together a rising young star and a brand looking to make its mark in one of beauty’s most exciting categories.

Adding to this, “India’s beauty consumers are evolving quickly, and the relevance of Korean beauty among young people continues to grow. With Mamonde, we are bringing innovative, benefit-led skincare to India at accessible price points. Nitanshi’s youthful energy and relatability make her the ideal face to introduce Mamonde to the next generation of beauty consumers. This appointment reflects our long-term commitment to building Mamonde into a strong Korean skincare brand in India,” shared Paul Lee, Managing Director & Country Head, Amorepacific India.

Meanwhile, “Mamonde brings together Korean skincare expertise, targeted formulations and a fresh approach to everyday beauty. With Nitanshi on board, we have an opportunity to bring the brand closer to young consumers through campaigns and conversations that feel relevant to them. From discovering products for specific skin concerns to finding new favourites for their everyday routines, we want to make exploring Mamonde an exciting experience for India’s young beauty community,” added Mini Sood Banerjee, Deputy Director, Amorepacific India.

Notably, The partnership also brings Mamonde’s philosophy, ‘Let Your Skin Bloom’, to life. Rooted in the resilience and transformative power of flowers, the philosophy celebrates the idea that beauty is never one-size-fits-all. Just as every flower blooms differently, every individual has unique skin needs. Mamonde encourages consumers to embrace that individuality and discover skincare that works for them.

As per the latest buzz, “I’m really excited to be joining Mamonde as its first brand ambassador in India. What drew me to the brand is how it combines Korean skincare innovation with a message that feels personal. ‘Let Your Skin Bloom’ is something I connect with because everyone’s skin is different, and skincare should be about discovering what makes you feel your best. I can’t wait to introduce more young people to Mamonde and be part of the brand’s journey in India,” shared Nitanshi Goel.

In further updates, Mamonde’s skincare range brings a targeted approach to everyday skin concerns. The Rose HA range, featuring a Serum and Sunscreen, focuses on hydration for a plump-looking, dewy complexion. The Peony BHA range, comprising a Serum and Sunscreen, addresses pore care and excess sebum management while providing UV protection. The range also features the Liquid Mask, a leave-on formula that combines gentle exfoliation with glow-enhancing benefits for an easy addition to everyday skincare routines.

On top of that, With its first brand ambassador now on board, Mamonde is set to introduce more Indian consumers to its take on Korean skincare, with Nitanshi helping bring its ‘Let Your Skin Bloom’ philosophy to life.

title: Nayyi Navelli review: Yami Gautam tries to hold together a fantasy film that thinks big, but barely makes sense
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Cast: Yami Gautam, Addinath Kothare, Sunita Rajwar, Mita Vashisht

Adding to this, The promotional material for Nayyi Navelli had one thing repeatedly mentioned: “Think big!” And so, with plenty of hope, I walked in to watch the movie, only to walk out wondering if the makers themselves had missed the memo.

Meanwhile, Directed by Balaji Mohan and written by Himanshu Sharma, the movie’s narrative is all over the place. Set in Meerut, it revolves around a man who accuses his bhabhi (played by Yami Gautam Dhar ) of being a witch, even while her husband and in-laws are fond of her. One day, her husband transforms into a monster, and we are told that it is all linked to Kaal Sheel, a mysterious stone dating back to the Treta Yuga. What follows is a heavy blend of mythology with humour.

Notably, The biggest problem is the screenplay, which lacks clarity and direction. The movie begins abruptly, leaving the viewer struggling to make sense of the events unfolding on screen. The narrative is further weighed down by a family of eccentric characters, most of whom alternate between delivering random one-liners and breaking into unnecessary shouting. The humour rarely feels organic, while the constant commotion does little to advance the story. At times, the movie feels less like a tightly written screenplay and more like an improvised series of scenes that have been strung together incoherently. The interval point feels like the movie's climax, and not in a good way.

As per the latest buzz, The second half thankfully picks up pace, introducing some interesting backstories that add some depth to the narrative. However, the respite is short lived, as Nayyi Navelli soon falls back into the same trap of excess. The movie struggles with restraint, stretching subplots and comic sequences well beyond their natural length. A track involving the marriage of a much older woman to a younger man, for instance, is given a lot of screen time without adding much to the narrative. If the intention is to extract a laugh or two, well, the sequence proves to be too flat to elicit even a chuckle.

In further updates, Among the performances, it's left to Yami to do the heavy lifting here. And she does well, to an extent. Without a solid story, how much can you expect an star to really perform? She has the presence and the emotional range, just not the material to make them both shine. The rest of the entire cast is strictly okay.
On top of that, The background score by GV Prakash Kumar helps occasionally, but also tends to get a bit loud. And the music, again by him, doesn't stand out.
The story is heavily reliant on VFX, and that is decent.

title: CID's Shivaji Satam recalls Nana Patekar fighting for his pay, stood by him during wife’s cancer battle: ‘Supported me like a real brother’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Shivaji Satam remembered Nana Patekar at a condolence meeting held in his honour. The gathering, titled ‘athvanitle Nana (Nana in our memories), was held at P.L. Deshpande Maharashtra Kala Academy complex in Prabhadevi in Mumbai, where several members of the movie industry came together to remember the star and the impact he had on their lives.

Adding to this, Shivaji Satam gets emotional remembering Nana Patekar, reveals how he stood by him during wife’s cancer battle. Shivaji remembered Nana and it meant looking back at nearly 40 years of friendship, countless personal memories and the support he received from the star at crucial moments in his life. He recalled how Nana encouraged him to take up Hindi films and even stepped in when he felt his friend was not being paid enough.

Meanwhile, Speaking at the prayer meet, Shivaji Satam, known as ACP Pradyuman from CID TV Show, shared, “Nana passed away so suddenly. When I heard the news, I honestly couldn't believe it. I have countless memories with Nana. We had known each other for nearly 40 years, and it was because of him that I found my footing in Hindi cinema. He was the one who pulled me into Hindi films. He convinced me, saying, ‘You should do this. You must do it.’"

Notably, Satam recalled that Nana was instrumental in getting him his first Hindi movie, Yashwant. “My first movie was Yashwant. The producer called me because there was a police officer's role in the movie, but I wasn't ready to take it up at the time. The producer told me that Nana Patekar, my friend, had recommended my name. When I refused, the producer called Nana, who then spoke to me in his own way and convinced me. Eventually, after saying no several times, I agreed," he revealed.

As per the latest buzz, He shared he was initially reluctant to take up the role of a police officer, but Nana personally convinced him to give it a shot. Their conversation did not end with the movie, though. When Nana later learnt how much Satam had been paid, he was upset that his friend had not consulted him before agreeing to the amount. “After the shoot was over, I met Nana again, and he asked me about the payment I had received. When I told him the amount, he got really angry. He shared, ‘You should have asked me at least once!’ He then scolded me, asking why I hadn't consulted him before accepting the payment. After that, he called the producers himself," the star further shared.

In further updates, Satam went on to share how Nana reacted when he learnt about the remuneration his friend had received. Even though Shivaji had asked him not to get involved, Nana was not willing to let the matter go. He wanted to make sure Satam was treated fairly and took it upon himself to speak to the producers.

On top of that, “I had specifically told him not to question the producers or speak to them about it. But Nana wouldn't listen. He made the producers stand for two hours, just like teachers used to make us stand in school. The poor producer stood there without saying a word," he revealed.

Shivaji's memories of Nana were not limited to their work together. One of the most difficult periods came when his wife was diagnosed with cancer while he was shooting for Ghulam-E-Musthafa. Unsure about how he would manage the movie alongside his family’s medical crisis, he considered stepping away from the project. Nana, however, made sure he did not have to deal with everything alone.

Adding to this, Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis among many other BJP leaders reacted to Bhushan’s 'regime change' remarks. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi alongside Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke , student organisation leaders and activists, Bhushan shared calls for regime change were part of democratic rights and that creating “disaffection” against a government was not a crime under the Constitution.

Meanwhile, “The government alleges the opposition wants a regime change... We are currently fighting to ensure that elections are conducted properly. But if this kind of brutality continues, there will certainly be regime change.
Notably, “What is wrong with that? BJP led several movements for regime change? Now they are saying there is a conspiracy for regime change...” Bhushan shared.
As per the latest buzz, “Regime change is the democratic right of every citizen. Creating disaffection for the government is not a crime as per our Constitution.
In further updates, “That is why this is now really a fight for regime change against a dictatorial government. A government that is crushing democracy,” he shared.

On top of that, Bhushan shared attempts by the authorities to suppress protests would only bring more people onto the streets. He added that young people would lead the movement for regime change, with civil society groups and political parties joining the campaign.

title: Press Council of India issues guidelines for journalists covering protests, stresses safety and neutrality
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Press Council of India (PCI) expressed concern over the safety of media personnel during unrest and rolled out a comprehensive set of guidelines for journalists covering protests and demonstrations, emphasising professional conduct, personal safety, and ethical reporting.

Adding to this, The advisory outlines strict protocols for personal protective measures, recommending compact emergency kits equipped with basic first aid, drinking water, high-protein snacks, flashlights, and eye protection/goggles. (ANI/ Representational) PCI notes that the guidelines seek to "facilitate the effective discharge of journalistic duties while promoting the safety of media personnel, responsible reporting and better coordination among journalists, media organisations and law enforcement authorities."

Meanwhile, Under the section on Identification and Professional Conduct, the Council has mandated that journalists carry valid identity cards issued by their media organisations or PIB/DIP accreditation, keeping them visibly displayed at all times via lanyards secured to minimise entanglement risks.

Notably, Highlighting the need for neutrality, the PCI guidelines state: "Maintain neutrality and professionalism. Do not participate in demonstrations, take sides, provoke confrontations, or interfere with protesters, counter-protesters, or police." Furthermore, journalists have been advised to remain respectful, comply with lawful police orders during tense situations, and avoid unnecessary arguments while calmly asserting their press status.

As per the latest buzz, Addressing positioning and crowd safety, the Council advised media persons to maintain a reasonable distance during escalating tensions or anticipated police action. It explicitly shared: "Do not attach cameras or recording equipment to police barricades, vehicles, or equipment in ways that obstruct movement or damage property."

In further updates, The advisory also outlines strict protocols for personal protective measures, recommending compact emergency kits equipped with basic first aid, drinking water, high-protein snacks, flashlights, and eye protection/goggles. Crucially, the guidelines warn: "Never touch, pick up, or attempt to move tear-gas canisters, flash-bang devices, or smoke grenades. They may remain hot, explode, or contain hazardous residue."

On top of that, Under ethical and responsible reporting, the PCI urged media professionals to verify information through multiple sources and treat statements from all quarters with equal scrutiny. Highlighting operational security and sensitivity, the Council directed: "Do not broadcast or publish real-time police positions, tactical movements, or escape routes when doing so could compromise safety or operational security." It also cautioned against letting exclusive footage pressures override fundamental safety considerations.

title: Will award compensation if Delhi protests impact traders, daily-wagers: Supreme Court
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Friday warned it would invoke its constitutional tort jurisdiction to award compensation if protests in Delhi disproportionately impede traders and daily-wage earners from pursuing their livelihoods, as it expressed concern over the hardship faced by small businesses during the festive season.

Adding to this, The court hoped that the situation would be handled with due regard for the economic vulnerability of small traders. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi made the remarks after a plea raised concerns over the proposed gathering at Central Park in Connaught Place by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), while hoping that “better sense will prevail” and that the competing interests of protesters, traders and the authorities would be balanced.

Meanwhile, “If there is loss of business, if it is unlawful to your clients, we will exercise our powers under constitutional tort jurisdiction. Let’s cross that bridge when it comes,” Justice Bagchi told advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai, who mentioned the petition on behalf of a traders’ association.

Notably, The court’s observations came a day after the Delhi High Court recorded an assurance from Delhi Police that it would take “all possible measures under the law” to regulate the proposed gathering and address apprehensions that it could disrupt business and movement in the Connaught Place area.

As per the latest buzz, Dehadrai told the Supreme Court that the proposed protest threatened substantial losses to traders, particularly when businesses depend on the festive season for a significant share of their earnings. He claimed that the disruption around Connaught Place was causing losses of more than ₹ 250 crore rupees a day.

In further updates, “This is also related to protest. It can wait till October 26,” CJI Kant shared initially, indicating that the matter would not be taken up immediately. Justice Bagchi pointed out that the Delhi High Court had heard a similar petition on Thursday.

On top of that, When counsel insisted that the plea before the Supreme Court raised distinct concerns, Justice Bagchi shared the competing claims of protesters, traders and law enforcement agencies had to be considered together.
“Someone wants to protest, someone wants to sell moongfali (peanuts), someone wants to maintain law and order. All are there before us. We can hear it after a week,” he shared.

title: Mahabharat actor Gajendra Chauhan says Imran Khan should be punished for participating in anti-CEC protest: ‘It is a violation of the law’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Gajendra Chauhan has also reacted strongly to the row, arguing that Imran, being an American citizen, should not have participated in the demonstration in Mumbai.

Adding to this, Gajendra Chauhan says Imran Khan should be punished. Gajendra Chauhan and Raza Murad react to Imran Khan getting leave India notice In conversation with ANI, the Mahabharat star shared that individuals residing in India on an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card are subject to certain restrictions and maintained that any violation of the law should invite appropriate action.

Meanwhile, Gajendra shared, “He is an American citizen, and he was living here. I don't think he should have gone to protest because it is against the law. If someone lives on an OCI card in India, he cannot fight the elections, cannot vote, and cannot protest. So, if he has done it, definitely he should be punished.”
Notably, He also questioned the time given to Imran to leave the country, suggesting that the authorities should act more swiftly.

As per the latest buzz, Expressing his disappointment, Gajendra added, “You have been such a big star in India. You have collected a name, collected money, collected a position. Indians used to love you. Despite that, you go to such a protest, which is against the residential values on which you are living in India. It is a violation of the law. And when there is a violation of the law, then the punishment will be there.”

In further updates, Veteran star Raza Murad also criticised Imran Khan, saying, “Whether it is Imran Khan or any other foreign national, there is no reason to interfere in the internal affairs of our country. Now I have come to know that Imran Khan has become a US national and he was an star here. So, as a US national, he has no right to intervene in the internal affairs of our country. Mumbai Police is doing this in the framework of the law. And he has not been told to leave the country tomorrow or in 24 hours. He has been given 15 days.”

title: Rajnath Singh attacks Congress over anti-CEC protests: ‘Conspiracy to grab power’
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Union defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday attacked the Opposition Congress over protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll, saying they raise serious questions. He accused the Opposition of wanting to push youth into anarchy to grab power.

Adding to this, Union defence minister Rajnath Singh shared institutions are being defamed and called it political opportunism (Deepak Gupta/HT Photo) “This fight is not for electoral reforms, not for SIR, not against Gyanesh Kumar, not for bright future of youth. It is a conspiracy to grab power. In democracy there is no licence to spread anarchy and attack constitutional institutions,” Singh shared in Lucknow .

Meanwhile, Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets seeking Kumar’s removal and the scrapping of SIR even as authorities ordered Metro closures, Internet shutdowns, imposed prohibitory orders and deployed 40,000 security personnel to turn Delhi into a virtual fortress. Many protesters were dragged, manhandled and detained as the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) blamed the Opposition for trying to deflect attention from its electoral failures.

Notably, Singh shared institutions are being defamed and called it political opportunism. “Rahul Gandhi should do introspection. This is my suggestion. We have chosen a path of dialogue, not confrontation, for nation building,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, He referred to the state of Emergency in the 1970s and the 1984 anti-Sikh riots as unpardonable crimes under the Congress patronage. He also cited the Congress’s role in saving the Samajwadi Party government after the 1990 firing on volunteers who converged on Ayodhya as part of the Ram temple campaign.

In further updates, Singh shared the Congress is committing the fourth unpardonable crime by hurting the Constitution, constitutional values and institutions. “In 1975 [Prime Minister] Indira Gandhi put democracy behind bars [during the state of Emergency]. Today Rahul Gandhi keeps the Constitution in his pocket and tries to spread anarchy,” Singh shared.

On top of that, He accused the Congress of making the Election Commission of India (ECI) its puppet. “There was a recommendation to remove Naveen Chawla as an election commissioner [in 2009] over the allegation that he shared information with Congress. Congress elevated him to the post of the chief election commissioner.”

Singh shared the Congress made former chief election commissioner MS Gill Union minister twice. “Until 1993, elections were held without voter IDs. Before 1993, there was no voter ID. There was no solid proof to establish voter identity. Since voter IDs were introduced, a majority has become a distant dream for Congress. Since the voter ID system was implemented, Congress has never formed a government,” he shared.

title: Why FRRO asked Imran Khan to leave India: The law, the notice, and the actor's options
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Mumbai has directed star Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, to leave the country by October 28, citing alleged violations of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.

Adding to this, Mumbai, Oct 10, 2026 – Police detain star Imran Khan among protesters at August Kranti Maidan during demonstrations supporting the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (HT File Photo/Raju Shinde) The FRRO, an agency under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), warned Khan that failing to comply with the directive would make him liable for criminal prosecution under immigration laws.

Meanwhile, The notice, issued on Thursday, has divided legal experts over the Union government's powers to deport the star for participating in a peaceful public demonstration, and the legal remedies available to him

Notably, On October 10, Khan joined a protest at August Kranti Maidan organised by Mahatma Gandhi’s great-grandson, Tushar Gandhi, supporting a campaign by Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP) demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

As per the latest buzz, Local police detained several participants, including Gandhi, Khan, his partner Lekha Washington, mother Nuzhat Khan, and cousin Zayn Marie, stating that the demonstration lacked prior police permission.

In further updates, In conversation with reporters before his detention, Khan shared, “I am here as a citizen, to see why freedom of movement has been restricted and why people’s voices are being oppressed.”
On top of that, Five days after the demonstration, the FRRO sent Khan a notice under the new Immigration and Foreigners Act, which took effect on September 1, 2025.

The legislation, which consolidated India’s immigration laws and strengthened provisions governing the entry, stay, and departure of foreign nationals, replaced four legacy statutes: the Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920; the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939; the Foreigners Act, 1946; and the Immigration (Carriers’ Liability) Act, 2000.

title: From Yami Gautam's Nayyi Navelli to Rajkummar Rao's Prahaar- Dusshera's big screen showdown set as 6 films battle it out
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

With Dussehra falling on October 20, the ticket-window is gearing up for a crowded festive weekend. While Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 opened on Thursday, Friday sees the rollout of Yami Gautam Dhar's fantasy drama Nayyi Navelli, Rajkummar Rao's courtroom drama a Pruhaa Pruhaar, Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna 's Ranabaali, and Hollywood films Street Fighter and Whalefall.

Adding to this, Stills from Prahaar, Nayyi Navelli Commenting on why the day matters to the trade, Kamal Gianchandani, CEO, PVR Inox Pictures Limited, tells us, “The Dussehra week is a very good window. It has always been a strong time to rollout a movie in all languages, not just Hindi but across the country. Typically, films rolled out during the Dussehra week have a very clean run until Diwali, when the next set of big films comes out. This gap of 20 days, which is roughly three weeks, is more than sufficient for films to have a very strong run at the ticket-window.” The Diwali rollout this time is Ramayana Part 1, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi, which releases on November 5.
Meanwhile, Kamal further feels that among the releases this week, Nayyi Navelli’s “goes well with the festival”, and Prahaar “is a high-concept movie… but anything can take off these days.”

Notably, As for the clash between films of various types this year, Devang Sampat, Managing Director, Cinepolis India says, “Six films in one week is a lot. There is room, because the audience grows during a festival and these films are in different languages and genres. But each one gets less time to find its audience. When a rollout date is planned with an eight-week view across languages, the movie gets a better run, audiences find it easier to decide, and we can plan our shows better.”

As per the latest buzz, Trade analyst Taran Adarsh echoes the same sentiment as he says, “There are going to be a lot of films this time. We can only hope that they all find an audience, because that’s the need of the hour. It will get more crowded from now on till Diwali.”

title: Imran Khan to challenge FRRO’s directive asking him to leave India by Oct 28; veteran Raza Murad slams him for taking part in protest
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The star is an American citizen and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder.

Adding to this, The star came under scrutiny following his participation in a protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Mumbai. The demonstration called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Meanwhile, Following the protest, BJP (Bharatiya Janata Party) leader Kirit Somaiya lodged a complaint with the police, alleging that Imran Khan’s participation in the demonstration violated the restrictions applicable to foreign citizens. The police subsequently forwarded the complaint to the FRRO, which issued a notice directing the star to leave the country.

Notably, The FRRO’s position is that holding an OCI card does not permit a foreign national to participate in protests. The order has been issued under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. Section 7 of the legislation empowers the Central Government to issue orders and directions regulating, restricting or prohibiting the entry, departure, presence or movement of foreign nationals in India.

As per the latest buzz, Meanwhile, veteran star Raza Murad has criticized Khan, asserting that foreign nationals should not interfere in India’s domestic affairs. He also defended the authorities’ handling of the matter, pointing out that the star has been given time to respond to the order and can seek judicial intervention if he believes the decision is unjust.

In further updates, “Whether it is Imran Khan or anyone else, no foreign national has any business interfering in the internal affairs of our country. I have only just learned that Imran Khan has become a U.S. national; he was an star here. As a U.S. national, he has no right to participate so actively in the country’s internal affairs or its politics. The Mumbai Police are acting strictly within the legal framework,” Murad told the news agency ANI.
On top of that, He further noted that the star has been given 15 days and can approach the court if he believes he is being treated unfairly or is being compelled to leave the country.

“He has been given a full 15 days. If he feels he is being treated unfairly or being forced to leave the country, he is welcome to approach the court, and whatever the court decides, we must all accept it. Let’s see how he reacts. He has two options: either leave the country by October 28, or if he does not wish to leave, or feels that he has been wronged or treated unjustly, he can take his grievance to the court,” Murad added.

title: Prahaar review: Rajkummar Rao shines in an interesting courtroom drama that occasionally loses focus
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Bollywood won’t let you forget 26/11. But neither would the memories.

Adding to this, A still from Prahaar. Nearly 18 years later, the tragedy continues to find its way to the big screen, with filmmakers exploring it through different perspectives. Kangana Ranaut’s Bharat Bhagya Vidhaata, rolled out earlier this year, was one such attempt. Now, the focus shifts to the courtroom and Ujjwal Nikam, the lawyer who prosecuted Ajmal Kasab, the lone terrorist captured alive during the Mumbai terror attacks. Starring Rajkummar Rao , Prahaar offers a different entry point into a story we know all too well. But does changing the vantage point change the story, too? Or is Bollywood once again banking on the gravity of history to do the heavy lifting? Let’s find out.

Meanwhile, The story begins with Nikam’s appointment as public prosecutor in the aftermath of the 26/11 attacks. As he builds a case against Kasab, he faces off against Abbas Kazmi (Sikandar Kher), the only lawyer willing to represent the captured terrorist. The movie also offers a glimpse into Nikam’s personal life, introducing his wife (Wamiqa Gabbi), son (Ritvik Sahore) and daughter, all of whom have had to contend with his prolonged absence as he throws himself into high-profile cases. How Nikam navigates the courtroom battle and ultimately seeks justice for the victims forms the rest of the story.

Notably, Director Avinash Arun, along with writer Sumit Roy, has zeroed in on an interesting subject. Prahaar is neither a conventional India vs Pakistan narrative nor one that relies on religious fault lines to make its point. The first half is crisp, establishing the tension effectively and moves towards a compelling interval point. There's also Jaideep Ahlawat as Pakistani prosecutor Zulfiqar Ali. That entire track (all of it true, by the way) is executed superbly. A special mention for the powerful dialogues by Sumit.
As per the latest buzz, It is in the second half, however, that it begins to lose its way.

In further updates, A movie like this did not need to devote so much time to Nikam’s family life. Yes, we need to understand who they are and what his demanding profession costs him personally. But given the enormity of the 26/11 attacks, the narrative would have benefited from keeping its focus firmly on the tragedy and the legal battle that followed, rather than repeatedly diverting attention towards Nikam’s attempts to balance his personal and professional lives. Two subplots, concerning his strained relationship with his son and his wife's health problems, occupy more screen time than they warrant. In trying to flesh out Nikam as a family man while also dramatising the courtroom proceedings, Prahaar ends up spreading itself too thin. What begins as a gripping legal drama gradually becomes an exhausting watch.
On top of that, There's also an unnecessary dramatic detour into Kasab's deteriorating mental health as he languishes in jail, adding little to the larger narrative.

What keeps you seated throughout is Rajkummar Rao. There are moments when you genuinely forget he is acting, and honestly, I am not sure there's a better way to describe how convincing he is. Wamiqa Gabbi gets the body language of an ageing woman spot on. Lalit Prabhakar, as Kasab, is effective in parts, while Sikandar Kher is simply too good. Ashish Vidyarthi, as the judge, makes his presence felt.

title: Kiss Ka Kissa: Vidhi Kasliwal announces romantic short film starring Priyanshu Painyuli and Vandana Josh
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Set in Mumbai, Kiss Ka Kissa explores the romantic dreams people carry from their younger days and the little moments that sometimes remain unfulfilled. Combining humour, affection and everyday situations, the movie looks at modern relationships and the ways romance can be found in seemingly ordinary experiences.

Adding to this, The pairing of Priyanshu Painyuli and Vandana Joshi, who are also a couple in real life, brings an element of familiarity to the story. Rather than relying on grand romantic gestures, the movie focuses on the emotions that emerge from everyday interactions. At its core, it celebrates spontaneity in love and the small moments that bring two people closer.

Meanwhile, For Vidhi Kasliwal, the project continues her interest in stories centred on human emotions. Her filmmaking journey includes working with Rajshri Productions alongside Sooraj R. Barjatya before making her writing and directorial debut with Isi Life Mein .

Notably, "What drew me to Kiss Ka Kissa was its simplicity. We often associate romance with grand gestures, but sometimes the smallest moments carry the deepest emotions. There is something wonderfully relatable about two people trying to find a little space for themselves in a city that never slows down. At Landmarc, we have always believed that stories don't need to be larger than life to touch lives. They simply need to feel real," says Vidhi Kasliwal.

As per the latest buzz, Written and directed by Ashish Sharma, Kiss Ka Kissa marks his fiction debut following more than a decade of work in advertising films, music videos and branded storytelling. The movie is presented by Landmarc Entertainment and produced under its Landmarc Films banner. Vidhi Kasliwal has handled the production and creative direction, while Aarti Bagdi serves as the creative producer.

In further updates, Speaking about the movie, Ashish Sharma shares, "I wanted to make Kiss Ka Kissa for two reasons: the little romantic dreams we carry from our younger days, and the joy of telling a simple, feel-good story. A first kiss, a stolen moment, a romantic adventure—sometimes life moves on, leaving these little dreams unfinished. Set against the chaos of Mumbai, the movie explores how even the simplest romantic gesture can become an adventure when privacy is a luxury. I wanted the humour to emerge naturally from everyday situations. At its heart, the movie celebrates love, youthful innocence and life's delightful unpredictability. I hope it leaves audiences smiling and perhaps remembering a little unfinished romantic story of their own."

On top of that, Over the past 15 years, Landmarc has developed a filmography that includes Sanngto Aika, Vazandar, Ringan, Gachchi, Redu, Pipsi, Nashibvaan and Medium Spicy . As the company transitions into Landmarc Entertainment, it is expanding its operations through three initial verticals: Landmarc Films, Landmarc Melodies and Landmarc Digital. The company aims to explore new storytelling formats and support new voices while continuing to focus on emotionally driven narratives.

The movie's creative team includes Vidhi Kasliwal as producer and creative visionary, Ashish Sharma as director, Aarti Bagdi as creative producer, Vikrant Thakur as director of photography and Puloma Pal as editor. Sarthak Karkare has composed the music, written the lyrics and created the background score. Prince Kumar of Casting Cubicle is responsible for casting, while K. R. Mahadevan [Mohan] serves as executive producer.

title: Drishyam 3 box office collection day 14: Ajay Devgn’s crime thriller witnesses a drop on 2nd Thursday amid competition from Jailer 2
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 14: After a strong run at the ticket-window, Ajay Devgn ’s Drishyam: The Conclusion is now witnessing a slowdown in collections as it enters its third week in theatres. The thriller has completed 14 days at the ticket-window and crossed ₹ 330 crore rupees in domestic net collections. However, with Rajinikanth ’s Jailer 2 arriving in cinemas and several more films set to rollout on Friday, the movie faces a tougher fight to maintain its momentum.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window earnings day 14: Ajay Devgn leads the thriller. Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Drishyam 3: The Conclusion collected an estimated ₹ 4.25 crore rupees net in India on Thursday, taking its total domestic collection to around ₹ 333.00 crore rupees. The movie recorded nearly 10% occupancy, with 10,797 shows.

Meanwhile, Thursday’s numbers were lower than Wednesday’s ₹ 5.25 crore rupees, marking a drop of around 42.5%. The decline comes as the movie enters its third week, when weekday collections typically begin to dip. Still, having crossed ₹ 330 crore rupees net in India, the movie has built a sizeable lead for itself. Its performance over the third weekend will show whether it can pick up pace again.

Notably, If the movie performs along these lines, it could collect another ₹ 20-25 crore rupees net over the weekend. That would take its India net total closer to ₹ 350 crore rupees. But, there is major competition when it comes to Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 which rolled out on October 15 and has already crossed ₹ 50 crore rupees mark and counting on the opening day.

As per the latest buzz, Drishyam 3 brings back Ajay Devgn’s Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav, and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also reprises his role from the second part in a cameo.

In further updates, Of late, Mohanlal , who plays Georgekutty in the original Malayalam Drishyam franchise, watched the Hindi movie and shared his appreciation for how the story has been wrapped up. The movie took a different route from the Malayalam version, and the veteran star's response is a significant moment for the team. Sharing a video, Mohanlal shared, “I watched Drishyam The Conclusion and I am truly impressed with the way they have brought much loved journey to a befitting end. Congratulations to Abhishek Pathak, Kumar Mangat Pathak, Ajay Devgn and the entire cast and crew on a job so well done.”

On top of that, An excerpt from Hindustan Times review read, “Drishyam: The Conclusion has enough drama and nostalgia to keep the followers engaged. But for a franchise that built its reputation on making the impossible seem plausible, this one asks us to take a few too many things at face value. It has the ingredients of a satisfying finale, just not the trick to pull it off. The mystery may finally be over, but the magic of the first Drishyam remains hard to recreate.”

title: Over 6,000 cops on duty, 50,000+ protesters expected: Delhi gears up for CJP march
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Delhi Police is going to deploy more than 6,000 police personnel in and around the Lutyens’ area ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) flag march (Tiranga Yatra) on October 16. Police shared they have already reserved 5,000 additional personnel from other districts and will guard the Rajiv Chowk area, Connaught Place markets, Central Park, nearby Metro stations, Jantar Mantar and Palika Bazaar.

Adding to this, In addition to the 6,000 personnel, the Delhi Police has deployed 220 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) (AFP) CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday revealed a Tiranga Yatra after his co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested on Tuesday morning and sent to five days of judicial custody for unfurling the national flag. Dipke, along with student organisations, activists and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), will participate in the march, which will start at 5 pm on October 16. Follow Delh protest LIVE updates

Meanwhile, Delhi Police PRO Neha Yadav shared there was no permission for the march and that police had already imposed Section 163 of the BNSS in the area. However, she shared permission could be given to a select few people to conduct a march at some other “suitable space”.
Notably, In addition to the 6,000 personnel, the Delhi Police has deployed 220 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) reserved for New Delhi, according to a senior police officers.

As per the latest buzz, “Out of the 220 companies, 30 companies will work in each shift. There will be three shifts during the day. They will be deployed in New Delhi, surrounding districts, borders and other important areas. If the crowd swells during the night and we need more security, we will increase the strength to 60 companies in one shift,” an officer shared.
In further updates, Police shared more than 10 CCTV cameras had been installed in and around the Central Park and Rajiv Chowk areas ahead of the march.

On top of that, “Since there were hardly any cameras at Central Park and a huge gathering of at least 30,000-50,000 people is expected, we have installed new cameras. The cameras are only there to record the gathering and collect evidence in case of any violations or untoward incidents,” the officer added.
HT also witnessed dozens of barricades lying along the streets near Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, ITO, Sansad Marg and other areas. Police had not blocked any roads as of Thursday evening.

title: Nushrratt Bharuccha undergoes spine surgery, discharged from hospital; team shares health update
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In a statement, her team shared, “After going through a difficult and challenging phase following her unfortunate accident, Nushrratt Bharuccha has successfully undergone spine surgery. We are relieved to share that the surgery went well, and she has now been discharged from the hospital.”

Adding to this, The statement added that Nushrratt is now at home, where she will focus on healing and regaining her strength. While her surgery was successful, her team noted that her recovery would take time.

Meanwhile, “Nushrratt is finally back home, surrounded by care and comfort, as she begins the important journey towards recovery. While the road to complete recovery will take time, she remains positive and is focusing on healing and regaining her strength,” the statement read.

Notably, Her team also thanked followers and well-wishers for their support during this period. “We sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming love, concern, prayers and good wishes extended to her during this difficult time,” the statement added.

As per the latest buzz, Nushrratt was on a work-cum-holiday trip to Bali when the accident occurred around October 1. Her team initially described the incident as an “unfortunate accident”, without disclosing details about its exact cause.

In further updates, Following the incident, the star was treated and kept under observation at a hospital in Bali. She was subsequently airlifted to Mumbai by air ambulance for further evaluation and corrective spine surgery.

On top of that, In the days following the incident, Nushrratt also shared glimpses of her recovery through Instagram Stories. One post featured a reclining wheelchair placed beside a window overlooking a sunset, accompanied by the caption, “Been chasing sunsets forever, And just like that… my view changed. But, Picture abhi baaki hai mere dost.”

In another update, the star shared a picture of herself smiling in bed while watching the song ‘ Gerua ’ from Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol’s movie Dilwale . The post carried the message, “Healing slowly, dreaming endlessly.”

title: Cockroach effigy to burn alongside Raavan's at Delhi's Ramlila Ground amid CJP protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

A 30-foot effigy of a cockroach will be set alight alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during a Ramlila event in Delhi this year, with organisers saying the insect symbolises filth and dirt.

Adding to this, The agitation eventually led to Pradhan's resignation as minister. (Anurag Mehra/ HT) The Shree Keshav Ram Leela Committee, which organises the annual event in Pitampura, shared the initiative was intended to promote cleanliness under the "Swachh Bharat" and "Swachh Delhi" campaigns.

Meanwhile, Committee president and BJP MLA Ashok Goel told news agency PTI that the decision was not driven by political considerations. He shared burning the effigy was meant to convey the message of good triumphing over evil while highlighting the importance of cleanliness.
Notably, The cockroach will also be depicted among the 'asuras' in Ravan's army, Goel shared.

As per the latest buzz, The decision comes as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has been holding protests in the national capital. The group initially demonstrated against former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and has now joined protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

In further updates, In June and July, CJP members staged a protest at Jantar Mantar for more than a month before marching to Parliament on July 20. The agitation eventually led to Pradhan's resignation as minister.

On top of that, The group has returned to the streets, joining opposition parties and student organisations in demonstrations seeking Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
The protests in Delhi have resulted in the detention of several activists, students and journalists.

title: Niti Taylor recalls casting couch ordeal with Telugu film director: “You will have to sleep with me for it this time”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The Kaisi Yeh Yaariaan star opened up that the disturbing phone call left her shocked and prompted her to step away from films.

Adding to this, Recounting the incident, Niti shared the director allegedly made an inappropriate demand in exchange for offering her another role. Describing how she reacted to the proposition, the star shared, "The director who did the first movie with me called me for another movie when we were done with it. Then he shared, 'But you will have to sleep with me for it this time.' You do not realise, you do not know how to react. I just cut the call, I blocked his number, I called up my mom, and I'm like, imagine that buddha, old man."

Meanwhile, Niti further explained that although she had previously noticed the filmmaker behaving in ways she found questionable around other women, she had not anticipated being subjected to such a proposition herself. The incident left her so shocked that she decided to distance herself from the movie industry.

Notably, Reflecting on how the experience affected her professional choices, she added, "I saw him with other chicks and stuff like that. I never knew when he would try this with me. That's when I decided I would never do any movies ever again. I was just taken aback, and I only blocked him. I did not tell this to anyone because I was zapped. You just come like..."

As per the latest buzz, Niti made her Telugu movie debut in 2012 with the romantic drama Mem Vayasuku Vacham , directed by Trinadha Rao Nakkina and produced by Bekkam Venugopal. Following the experience she described, the star shifted her focus towards television, where she went on to establish herself as a familiar face among Indian audiences.

In further updates, She rose to widespread popularity for playing Nandini Murthy in the youth-oriented series Kaisi Yeh Yaariaan, opposite Parth Samthaan. The show's popularity led to multiple subsequent seasons, further strengthening her fan following. Over the years, Niti has also appeared in television shows including Ghulaam, Ishqbaaaz and Bade Achhe Lagte Hain 2. She was last seen in the Amazon Prime Video reality series Alliance.

On top of that, Her latest account offers a glimpse into the difficult experiences she says shaped her early career and influenced her decision to concentrate on television rather than pursue further movie projects at the time.

title: Madhuri Dixit and Shriram Nene celebrate 27th anniversary with rare photos from their Beverly Hills wedding: ‘To infinity and beyond, together'
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Dr Shriram Nene has a special reason to look back at his wedding album. The cardiovascular surgeon marked 27 years of marriage with star Madhuri Dixit by sharing rare photographs from their wedding and celebrations with family and friends. Along with the pictures, he penned a sweet note about their life together, reflecting on the memories, challenges and happiness they have shared over the years.

Adding to this, Madhuri Dixit and Dr Shriram Nene mark 27 years of marriage with rare wedding photos. Shriram Nene shares rare pictures with Madhuri Dixit The photographs offer a glimpse into the couple's early days together, including moments from their ring exchange and celebrations with loved ones. Looking back at their wedding at the Beverly Hills courthouse in California, Shriram wrote, “27 years ago today, at the Beverly Hills courthouse, we shared 'I do' and began the adventure of a lifetime. We had no idea where life would take us, but we knew we wanted to experience it together. Two incredible sons, countless memories, a few challenges, lots of laughter, and a lifetime of love later, I'd choose you all over again.”

Meanwhile, He added, “Here's to the beautiful journey we've shared and all the chapters still to come. Happy 27th anniversary, my love. To infinity and beyond, together. #27YearsTogether #HappyAnniversary”.

Notably, View this post on Instagram How Madhuri Dixit and Dr Nene's love story began Madhuri and Shriram married in a private ceremony in California in 1999. Sriram, who grew up in the United States and worked as a cardiovascular surgeon, as per reports did not know much about Madhuri's stardom when they first met through her brother.

As per the latest buzz, After the wedding, Madhuri moved to Denver, Colorado, where he was building his medical career. The couple welcomed their first son, Arin, in March 2003, and their second son, Ryan, in March 2005. Madhuri took a break from full-time acting during this period to focus on motherhood and family life.

In further updates, Of late, filmmaker and choreographer Farah Khan visited Madhuri and Shriram at their home for her latest cooking vlog, accompanied by her cook, Dilip. During the conversation, he opened up that he felt like a prom king at their wedding reception because he did not know any of the celebrities who attended, apart from Amitabh Bachchan. He shared, “I didn't know anyone. It was like Prom King, you just waved at everyone and later look at the wedding album because you don't know anyone. The only person I knew was Amitabh Bachchan because I had seen Amar Akbar Anthony.”

On top of that, She returned to films with Aaja Nachle in 2007. A few years later, in 2011, the family moved back to India, and Madhuri gradually returned to taking on more acting projects. Since then, she has worked across films, television and streaming, continuing to remain a familiar face to audiences. She is currently hosting Kon Honar Crorepati , Marathi version of Kaun Banega Crorepati.

title: International fans go gaga over new Ramayana trailer featuring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's grand face off as Lord Rama and Ravana: ‘Avatar-level movie’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The international trailer of Ramayana : Rise of a Legend is finally here, giving audiences their spectacular new glimpse of Nitesh Tiwari’s ambitious take on one of India’s most celebrated epics. Starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, the movie brings together a celebrated cast, large-scale visuals and music by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer.

Adding to this, Ramayana international trailer gives a fresh glimpse of Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s face-off, followers can't keep calm. The trailer introduces a world of gods, demons, duty and sacrifice, setting up the battle between Rama and Ravana. With sweeping landscapes and dramatic moments, the movie aims to bring the timeless story to life for a new generation of moviegoers while retaining the epic's central conflict between good and evil.

Meanwhile, The 2-minute 36-second trailer shows new footage and more moments featuring Ram and Ravana. The trailer opens with a voice describing a time when the world lived in harmony, saying, “Before history was written... men walked among gods... and the world existed in perfect order.” It finally shows Kunal Kapoor playing the role of Lord Indra. That peace is soon threatened by Ravana, whose rise to power changes the course of the world. The narration continues, “But from the darkness rose an evil force... Ravana. Born from fire and fury, he bent the gods to his will and made the world his throne.”

Notably, Played by Yash, the King of Lanka makes his intentions clear with the chilling declaration, “Before me, every head will bow...” As Ravana's power grows, the story turns to Rama, presented as the one person who can stand against him. The voice explains, “In this time of peril, humanity had one hope. Not a god, but a man, chosen by destiny: Ram.”

As per the latest buzz, Ranbir Kapoor's Rama is shown grappling with the responsibility that comes with his destiny. Determined to stop Ravana, he says, “If this is my fate... I will not hesitate to destroy him. If I don't stop him... the world will fall.” The trailer closes on a foreboding note, with Ravana warning, “This is just... the beginning.”

In further updates, The trailer received an enthusiastic response from viewers on X, with many praising its visuals, scale and music. One user was particularly impressed by the score heard towards the end, writing, “That shyama shyama score in the end. Mann, Hans Zimmer you are the GOAT fr.” Another declared, “Bow down to INDIAN CINEMA.” A third wrote, “Words are less to define what they have made⚡Can't wait to experience this!!” Comparing the movie's scale to other major cinematic spectacles, another user shared, “People were comparing the Ramayana with the Odyssey but I’m telling you, it’s looking like Avatar level movie. This will rock in ticket-window.”

On top of that, International audiences reacting to the trailer on X were impressed by its scale and visuals. One user wrote, “This looks spectacular. This is supposed to be the first part. It carries a $250m budget. Will probably have another $150m for marketing. Part of has the same budget.” Another viewer expressed excitement about Indian mythology getting a grand cinematic treatment, writing, “Wake the fk up, Indians literally made Avatar Lotr level shit. Hindu epics are absolutely insane and still unexplored." Another X user wrote, " This movie is apparently 3 hours and 30 minutes??? People saying it's Endgame level."

The first trailer had drawn criticism from some viewers for its visual effects, sparking debate about the movie's CGI and overall look. The team has urged audiences to wait for the finished movie and experience it in theatres before reaching a final verdict. But the fresh new English international trailer shows the movie as a massive epic.

title: Central Park in Delhi's Connaught Place shut for two days as court refuses to block Abhijeet Dipke's protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
The New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) on Thursday opened up that Central Park in Connaught Place would remain closed to the public on Friday and Saturday, citing administrative reasons.

Adding to this, Abhijeet Dipke called for a ‘Tiranga March’ at Central Park in Delhi’s Connaught Place on October 16. (AFP) The decision comes a day after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke called for a “Lehra Do Tiranga” (Let the Tricolour Fly) demonstration at the park on October 16. The park’s closure comes after the Delhi High Court declined to restrain the CJP from holding the protest. The Delhi police told the court that it would take all possible measures to maintain order.

Meanwhile, In a public notice issued on October 15, the civic body shared, “It is hereby informed that the Central Park, Connaught Place shall remain closed for general public on 16th October and 17th October due to administrative reason.”
Notably, Senior NDMC officials declined to comment on the reasons behind the closure of the park, which is located in the heart of Connaught Place.
As per the latest buzz, Dipke has urged people to gather at the park with the national flag at 5 pm on Friday as part of the proposed demonstration.

In further updates, Located above the Rajiv Chowk Metro station, Central Park is spread across 41,500 square metres and features four water bodies, a 350-seat amphitheatre and a monumental Indian flag mounted on a 207-foot-high mast. The NDMC’s horticulture department maintains the park.

On top of that, An NDMC official, speaking on condition of anonymity, shared the civic body had received instructions from senior authorities to close the park. All five gates will be shut, the official added.

The park’s amphitheatre is often booked for government functions and social and cultural programmes, while the green space attracts large numbers of visitors, particularly on weekends, the official shared.

title: Kirti Kulhari’s production debut Kinaare to premiere at Dharamshala International Film Festival
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Written and directed by the Qadri brothers (Akbar & Azam Qadri), Kinaare will premiere at DIFF and it marks a deeply personal chapter for Kulhari as she steps into the role of a producer. She has backed the feature under her banner Kintsukuroi Films along with co-producers Abhishek Koka and Maansi Guptey.

Adding to this, Set against the backdrop of a village near Delhi, Kinaare follows Amina (played by Kulhari), a single woman whose life is devoted to caring for her aging parents and tending to her home. Her routine is upended by a surprise visit from her cousin brother (Azam) after 15 years—unearthing a past that once fractured the family. Catching up on lost years—and love—the visit leaves her more at peace with the past and acceptance of the present.

Meanwhile, Reflecting on the creative energy that went into shaping the project, lead star and producer Kulhari shared, “ Kinaare is a movie that happens to be my first child as a producer, and that will always remain special. It’s a script that really resonated with me. It’s a simple, heartwarming, and subtle movie. I find all these adjectives in Iranian films—which I’ve always really loved—so when something like this came to me, I knew I had to make it.”
Notably, Kulhari, who comes armed with more than a decade of a stellar acting career, shared producing is not an easy task, especially if one’s trying to make a movie themselves.

As per the latest buzz, “This is exactly how I wanted to make this movie: independently, make it the way I see it, the way we all see it collectively. It’s amazing that each and every member of the movie has come together, believing in the script, and stood by my side purely for the passion of cinema, for the sole reason of being a part of the movie for what it is. So, I’m very proud and happy to have brought something like Kinaare for the world to see.”
In further updates, Echoing this sentiment, co-star Rajeev Siddhartha opened up about the rare rhythm of the script and the immersive environment on set.

On top of that, “I feel every star looks forward to and hopes that they come across a script where not only is the written word important, but also the script itself encourages you to explore the spaces between the words. And with Kinaare , I got to do that as an star. I feel Kinaare has such a universal theme that everybody who sees it will definitely be touched, be moved and be slightly changed from within after the experience.”

title: ‘You are trying to create unrest’: Ashoke Pandit backs government notice to Imran Khan to leave India, questions his right to protest as US citizen
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Ashoke Pandit has backed the government's decision to ask star Imran Khan to leave India after his participation in a Mumbai protest sparked a political row. He questioned the star's decision to join the demonstration, arguing that a foreign national who is not an Indian citizen cannot claim the right to protest in the country. Imran, who holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card and is a US citizen, is now preparing to challenge the government's notice in the Bombay High Court.

Adding to this, ‘First educate yourself’: Ashoke Pandit’s sharp message to Imran Khan after Mumbai protest row. What Ashoke Pandit shared “I am really very happy… because when you don’t have a right to protest, and you are not a citizen of this country. You go all out to see to it that our country is defamed,” Ashoke Padnit told ANI in an interview.

Meanwhile, He also urged Imran to understand the rules governing his status before taking part in a demonstration. He added, “So, first educate yourself, study, and ask your family members and elders to explain whether you are allowed to take to the streets and wage a war against this country, because you are trying to create unrest in the country”.

Notably, View this post on Instagram Why was Imran Khan asked to leave India? The row began on October 10, when Mumbai Police detained Imran, nephew of star Aamir Khan , during a protest at August Kranti Maidan. Organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the demonstration called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
As per the latest buzz, After his detention, the star shared a photograph that appeared to show him inside a police van, with the caption, “Apparently I’m going for a drive”.

In further updates, In conversation with the media at the protest, the star shared he had joined the demonstration as someone who lives in Mumbai. “I don’t have demands. I’m here as a citizen, as a person who lives in this city. I’m here to see why freedom of movement is being restricted, why people’s voices are being suppressed,” he shared.

On top of that, On October 15, the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) issued a notice directing Imran to leave India by October 28. The notice cited alleged violations of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.

The star's lawyer, Zulfikar Memon, has verified that the star will challenge the notice in the Bombay High Court. The petition is expected to be filed by Friday or Monday. His legal team has described the order as “drastic” and argued that no provision of the law specifically bars OCI cardholders from participating in protests.
